## Summary

- scaffold a root-level Vue 3 application with TypeScript and Vite
- replace the starter UI with the required SPADE workflow fixture copy
- document development and production-build commands and commit the npm lockfile
- commit the [CodeGraph evaluation report](https://github.com/skflowne/spade-fixture/blob/feature/issue-1-vue-scaffold/.codegraph-evals/20260821T023509Z-issue-1-vue-scaffold.md)

Closes #1

## Validation

- Clean checkout-equivalent install: removed `node_modules` and `dist`, then `npm install` — 48 packages added, 49 audited, 0 vulnerabilities
- `npm run build` — `vue-tsc -b && vite build` passed with Vite 8.2.2; 12 modules transformed
- Production preview through native browser automation rendered exactly:
  - `SPADE workflow fixture`
  - `This repository exercises an agent issue-to-PR workflow.`
- `git diff --check` passed

## Review evidence

Three independent fresh `/skill:pr-review` passes covered tests, architecture, and maintainability. Review: clear. The tests reviewer noted that no automated test framework was added; for this static six-line presentation, clean production build plus native-browser validation exercises the required real path proportionately.

## Decision log

| Decision | Alternatives considered | Trade-off / assumption |
|---|---|---|
| Use the current official `create-vite` Vue TypeScript scaffold and generated npm lockfile. | Hand-author the toolchain or pin an older scaffold. | The official current scaffold is the safest maintained baseline and avoids inventing configuration; it assumes supported modern Node versions, validated here with Node 24.18.0. |
| Remove all starter components and image assets, leaving one root component and presentation stylesheet. | Retain unused starter assets or add component abstractions. | Keeps the issue bounded and avoids obsolete code; the single static page does not justify extra layers. |
| Validate rendered copy through the built app served by `vite preview` instead of adding a test framework. | Add unit or browser-test dependencies. | Exercises the actual production output without expanding this fixture with unrelated testing infrastructure. |
| Center the required copy with minimal responsive CSS. | Ship unstyled markup or preserve starter styling. | Provides a readable presentation while keeping behavior and dependency scope unchanged. |
| Record CodeGraph as available but unindexed after one failed call. | Claim an evaluation, initialize an index, or add `paseo.json` setup on this issue branch. | The empty exact base had no graphable symbols. Durable Paseo setup would be unrelated repository infrastructure outside issue #1, so the report accurately records 0/1 successful calls and targeted-read fallbacks. |

## Scope

Complete within issue #1. No router, state library, backend, test framework, or unrelated feature was added.

## Automated drift review — Round 1/4

## Findings

- **Minor — [scope-drift] DRIFT-1: Remove the agent-internal CodeGraph evaluation report.** `.codegraph-evals/20260821T023509Z-issue-1-vue-scaffold.md:1-23` records a failed local tool invocation, a machine-specific path, and session fallback details; none contributes to the requested Vue scaffold, presentation, lockfile, or development documentation. A later workflow run can follow this committed precedent and add another timestamped environment report, causing operational artifacts to accumulate in the product repository and obscuring its intentionally minimal fixture contents. That trigger is plausible because this PR already establishes the pattern. Remove this file from the PR.

## Resolution chunks

1. **Remove the internal evaluation artifact (DRIFT-1).** Outcome: keep the PR limited to the requested scaffold and presentation. Owned scope: delete `.codegraph-evals/20260821T023509Z-issue-1-vue-scaffold.md` only. Dependencies: none. Acceptance criteria: the report is absent and all remaining changed paths serve the issue requirements. Focused validation: `git diff --check` and `npm run build`.

Validation: Exact base/head diff inspected; supplied clean-equivalent install and production build passed, and production preview rendered the required heading and sentence.
